title: Approval for Undischarged Bankrupts to File Employment Dispute with Tripartite Alliance for Disputes Management
what_it_is: Approval for Undischarged Bankrupts to File Employment Dispute with Tripartite Alliance for Disputes Management

sections.label: Bankrupt worker salary claims
sections.summary: An undischarged bankrupt with unpaid salary needed approval to take a claim to the Employment Claims Tribunals after mediation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: If the mediation at the TADM is unsuccessful, the claimant will be issued with a claim referral certificate with which he may then file a claim at the Employment Claims Tribunals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: If he chooses to do so, under the Bankruptcy Act or the Insolvency, Restructuring and Dissolution Act 2018, whichever is applicable, the bankrupt needs to apply to the OA or a private trustee in bankruptcy for a sanction.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: This requirement exists to protect the bankruptcy estate and hence, the interests of the bankrupt’s creditors, from costs that may be incurred by the bankrupt bringing or defending actions that are frivolous or legally unmeritorious.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: One of the residents in my Pioneer single member constituency (SMC), who is an undischarged bankrupt, had salaries  including overtime payments owing to him.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: As the Senior Parliamentary Secretary rightly pointed out, after mediation, he still needed the approval of MinLaw to be able to take the claim to the Employment Claims Tribunals.

sections.label: Reviewing approval process for workers
sections.summary: A speaker hoped the Ministry of Law would review the approval process, and the Ministry said it would take the point back.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: So, it is a bit ironical that in late payment or unpaid salary situations, he or she is unable to take further action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Therefore, I hope the Ministry of Law can review this to make the process more seamless and easier for aggrieved workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: I appreciate the point raised and perhaps what may be useful is to also understand the specific case in concern.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: There is that approval process and if it does appear that there is likelihood of success, it is something for the agency to think about.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: But I do appreciate the point made that this may be a bit challenging.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We will take this back to see how we can facilitate the process even better.
